label: Test Case, Answered Last
line: Pose one famous concrete case in the first sentence, walk the rules from easiest to hardest, and answer the case in the last sentence.
best_for: a system of rules: address ranges, permissions, licences, types, the rules of a story's world
a 'would this count as that' question
also_for: a classification with no order, followed through one example
avoid_for: a case with no definite answer
rules that are guesses: each needs a source
a case the audience does not know
signals: the topic is a system of rules
one famous concrete case tests the rules
the rules can be walked from easy to hard
the case has a definite answer
a named source settles the part of the rules the case turns on

beats.name: The case
beats.job: Would this famous concrete case count? Asked in the first sentence.

beats.name: Fair question
beats.job: Why the question is a reasonable one.

beats.name: Rules, easiest first
beats.job: One rule per sentence, with one 'you would think so, but' among them.

beats.name: Where the rules run out
beats.job: The part of the rules that does not settle the case at first, and the source that does.

beats.name: Precedent
beats.job: A known case the rules did settle.

hooks.shape: What if [famous case] had to follow the rules of [system]?
Everyone says [famous case] is [category]. The rules say something else.

holds: The case is on screen from the first second and is not answered until the last, so every rule is heard as evidence for or against it.
ending: The case's answer. Nothing after it.
first_frame: The concrete case on screen from the first second, drawn so the same picture can come back for the answer.
pitfalls: Rules listed with no case to test them on
A hedge where the answer belongs
template: Would [concrete case] count as [category]? Fair question. [Category 1] is easy: [rule]. You would think [category 2] means [naive reading], but [real rule]. Then there is [the part the rules leave open], which [source] settles: [what it says]. Proof: [a known case]. Which makes [concrete case] [answer].
